answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Most common lethal skin cancer; responsible for the majority of skin cancer deaths.
- Defined by malignant proliferation of melanocytes with rapid progression and metastatic potential.
- Breslow depth is the most important prognostic and staging criterion.
- UV exposure (especially intermittent intense sunburns) is the major risk factor.
- Pathology checklist: asymmetry, lack of maturation, pagetoid scatter, atypical/deep mitoses, and ulceration.

## Terminology

- Defined as a malignant melanocytic tumor arising from melanocytes of the skin [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Synonyms (ICD-O): malignant melanoma, NOS (8720/3), superficial spreading melanoma (8743/3), lentigo maligna melanoma (8742/3), nodular melanoma (8721/3), desmoplastic melanoma (8745/3), among others [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Outdated/not recommended: "melanose," "fungoid disease" [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**
  - Malignant cytology: nuclear pleomorphism and enlargement (>1.5x basal keratinocytes), hyperchromasia, atypical mitotic figures [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Coarse irregular chromatin with peripheral condensation ("peppered moth nuclei") [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Asymmetry, ill-defined border, and complex/irregular nests [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Lack of maturation (no decrease in cell/nest size with depth) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Pagetoid spread: melanocytes scattered throughout all layers of the epidermis (especially in superficial spreading type) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Invasion of dermis (radial and/or vertical growth phase) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Breslow depth must be measured from the top of granular layer (or base of ulcer if present) to the deepest malignant cell [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Mitoses, including deep dermal mitotic activity (>1/mm²) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Ulceration and absence or nonbrisk tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes are staging criteria [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- **Desirable:**
  - Immunohistochemistry confirming melanocytic lineage (S100, Melan-A, SOX10, HMB-45) in challenging cases [Dermal melanoma, WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html).
  - Molecular characterization (e.g., BRAF, NRAS, KIT) for advanced disease management [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- Multistep oncogenic process involving environmental (UV) and genetic factors [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Initiating mutation (BRAF or NRAS), escape from senescence (CDKN2A loss), apoptosis resistance (TP53 mutation), and immortalization (TERT promoter mutation) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- UV exposure is the main cause (including intense intermittent exposure or artificial UV) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Genetic risk: germline mutations in CDKN2A, CDK4, MITF, TERT, ACD, TERF2IP, POT1, MC1R, BAP1 [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- High CSD (chronic sun-damaged) melanomas: lentigo maligna, desmoplastic, H-CSD nodular [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Low CSD: superficial spreading, L-CSD nodular [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Subtypes not linked to CSD: Spitz, acral, mucosal, those arising in congenital or blue nevi [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Can arise de novo or from pre-existing nevus [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Clinical Issues

  - **Epidemiology:**
    - Incidence: 3.2 age-standardized rate (worldwide); ~1.7% of global cancer [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
    - Incidence is rising rapidly; higher in periequatorial zones [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
    - M:F ratio ≈ 1.5:1 [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - **Site:**
    - Can occur anywhere on the skin, including subungual locations [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
    - Frequent on trunk, lower extremities, and, for lentigo maligna, face and chronically sun-exposed sites [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - **Presentation:**
    - Flat, slightly elevated, nodular, polypoid, or verrucous pigmented lesion; may be amelanotic [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
    - ABCDEs: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation (>4 colors), Diameter >6 mm, Evolving [Derm Mckee](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1238).
    - Ugly duckling sign, Hutchinson sign, and blowfly sign recognized as notable patterns [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - **Natural History:**
    - Aggressive—high potential for local recurrence, nodal, and distant metastasis.
    - Most arise de novo; minority develop on a nevus [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - **Treatment:**
    - Wide surgical excision with margins determined by Breslow depth: in situ (0.5 cm), ≤2 mm (1 cm), >2 mm (2 cm) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
    - Sentinel lymph node biopsy for staging and prognosis [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
    - Adjuvant/systemic therapy (immune checkpoint inhibitors, targeted agents) from stage III [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - **Complications:**
    - Local recurrence, nodal and visceral metastasis, treatment-related morbidity.
    - Prognosis excellent when localized and excised (5-year survival 100%), decreases with nodal (75%) and distant mets (35%) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Staging

- AJCC TNM system for all cutaneous melanomas [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanomastaging.html).
  - pT staged by Breslow depth (top granular layer/base of ulcer to deepest tumor cell) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanomastaging.html).
  - pN: nodal metastasis (clinically occult/detected microscopically) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanomastaging.html).
  - pM: Distant metastasis [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanomastaging.html).
  - Stage IA: T1a N0 M0; IIC: T4b N0 M0; IV: any T, any N, M1 [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanomastaging.html).
  - Additional factors: ulceration, mitotic rate, sentinel node status.

## Macroscopic

- Variable presentation: flat, slightly raised, nodular, polypoid, or verrucous lesions [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Irregularly pigmented, often with >4 colors and asymmetrical shape.
- May present as achromic (amelanotic) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Tumor size >6 mm typical, but smaller "micromelanomas" (<2 mm) also occur [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Ulceration, regression, or satellite nodules may be present.

## Microscopic

- Asymmetrical silhouette, ill-defined lateral borders at low power.
- **Epidermal component:**
  - Pagetoid spread: single melanocytes in upper layers of epidermis (especially SSM) ![Pagetoid spread](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/images/skin/pagetoid%20extension.jpg)
  - Confluent proliferation at the junction, irregular nests of varying size/shape [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Irregular distribution of melanocytes at the dermal-epidermal junction.
  - Epidermal consumption and ulceration may be seen ![Ulceration](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati16.jpg)
- **Dermal component:**
  - Vertical growth phase: expansile dermal nest larger than all junctional nests [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Lack of maturation: persistence of large/atypical nests and cells in deep dermis.
  - Expansile (sheet-like) growth, often with a lack of circumscription.
  - High mitotic rate, including atypical and deep dermal mitoses.
  - Cytology: epithelioid and/or spindle-shaped cells with pleomorphism, enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, coarse chromatin with peripheral condensation ("peppered moth nuclei"), prominent nucleoli [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Stromal changes: variable inflammatory (lymphoid) infiltrate, which may be brisk, nonbrisk, or absent [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Ulceration and regression, along with neurotropism and lymphovascular invasion in some cases.
- **Special subtypes:**
  - Superficial spreading: nested and pagetoid growth, marked pagetoid scatter, junctional and dermal proliferation ![Superficial spreading melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati01.jpg)
  - Nodular: predominantly vertical growth, little/no in situ/radial phase ![Nodular melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati003.jpg)
  - Acral lentiginous: lentiginous proliferation, often acral location ![Acral lentiginous melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati04.jpg)
  - Desmoplastic: spindle cells, abundant collagen, may lack pigment ![Desmoplastic melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati06.jpg)
  - Lentigo maligna: confluent lentiginous junctional proliferation.
- **Other features:** Confluent nests, poorly differentiated patterns, ill-defined margins, and necrosis (occasionally) ![Confluent nests](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati15.jpg), ![Poorly differentiated melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati13.jpg).

## Ancillary Tests

- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - S100 protein: sensitive but not specific [Dermal melanoma, WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html).
  - Melan-A (MART-1), SOX10, HMB45: confirm melanocytic origin [Dermal melanoma, WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html).
  - Ki-67: may help assess proliferation.
- **Molecular genetics:**
  - BRAF V600E mutations common (especially in low CSD, young/middle age) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
  - Other pathway mutations: NRAS, KIT, TERT promoter, CDKN2A, and others.
  - BRAF testing recommended for Stage III-IV melanomas for therapeutic selection.
- **Laboratory findings:**
  - Increased serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is associated with advanced/metastatic disease [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Differential Diagnosis

- **Dysplastic (Atypical) Nevus (Clark nevus):**
  - Usually smaller, symmetrical, with zone of maturation with depth.
  - Nuclear atypia less uniform; pagetoid scatter, mitosis, or deep atypia absent or focal [Derm Levers](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_Levers.pdf#page=180).
- **Combined or Congenital Nevus:**
  - Maturation with depth, lack of deep mitotic activity.
- **Proliferative Nodule in Congenital Nevus:**
  - Expansile dermal nodule within nevus, minimal pleomorphism, rarely metastasizes [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticproliferativenodule.html).
- **Recurrent Nevus:**
  - Atypical lentiginous proliferation over scar; no deeper invasion, limited atypia [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Recurrent_Naevus.html).
- **Halo Nevus:**
  - Lichenoid infiltrate; melanoma favored by expansile growth, severe atypia, high mitotic rate, ulceration [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Halo_Naevus.html).
- **Spitz Nevus/Atypical Spitz Tumor:**
  - Large spitzoid cells, benign symmetry, and maturation; lack high-grade cytologic atypia and deep mitoses.
- **Blue Nevus / Cellular Blue Nevus:**
  - Dendritic spindle cells, symmetry, low mitotic index; blue nevus-like melanoma has atypia, mitotic activity [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnevigeneral.html).
- **Mucosal melanoma:**
  - Arises on mucosal surfaces, has distinct clinicopathologic and molecular features [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Mucosal_Melanoma.html).
- **Atypical naevus:**
  - May share some histological atypia, but lacks the full malignant architecture and cytology of invasive melanoma [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html).
- **Primary dermal melanoma:**
  - Confined to the dermis, must be distinguished from cutaneous metastases and other blue nevi; shares immunophenotype with classic melanoma [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html).
- **Other non-melanocytic mimics:**
  - Amelanotic melanoma may mimic SCC, appendageal tumors, sarcomas, cutaneous lymphoma; diagnostic IHC required [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Nodular_Melanoma.html).
- **Metastatic melanoma:**
  - May mimic primary cutaneous melanoma; clinical correlation and sometimes molecular workup needed [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html).

## Prognostic Factors

- Breslow depth: primary determinant of staging and prognosis—measured to deepest cell [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Ulceration: worsens stage and survival [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Sentinel lymph node positivity: adverse outcome [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- High dermal mitotic rate: poor prognosis [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes: brisk is favorable; absent/nonbrisk is unfavorable [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Increasing angiogenesis (VEGF, D2-40) linked to higher relapse and death; molecular findings (e.g., BRAF) may also impact prognosis [Derm Mckee](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/Derm_McKee.pdf#page=1252).
- 5-year survival: localized 100%, regional 75%, metastatic 35% [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Recurrence rate (high risk melanoma): ~13% within 2 years [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Subtype: pure desmoplastic and Spitz-related melanomas can have more favorable prognosis [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Illustrative Cases

- Lesions can present at a wide age range and multiple sites (e.g., subungual, scalp, ear, foot, thorax, arm, scapula, forehead) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Clinical variability includes irregularly pigmented or amelanotic nodules, verrucous/scalp lesions, and lesions arising in nevi [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

cards.title: Halo naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Halo naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis of involuting halo naevi includes other lichenoid interface reactions, such as those seen in lichenoid keratosis and melanoma with lichenoid inflammation. Findings suggestive of melanoma include the presence of a separate population of cells with an expansile pattern of growth; severe cytological atypia; and frequent mitoses, ulceration, or tumour necrosis. The halo phenomenon may occasionally involve other types of naevi, including dysplastic, Spitz, and congenital naevi, as well as melanomas. In most lesions, there is no intraepidermal melanocytic proliferation adjacent to the dermal component. If in situ or superficially invasive melanoma is present adjacent to a dermal lesion simulating halo naevus, the entire lesion is most likely melanoma.

cards.title: Recurrent naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Recurrent naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis includes melanoma, dysplastic naevus, sclerosing naevus, and dysplastic naevus with florid fibroplasia.

cards.title: Mucosal melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mucosal melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis includes dysplastic naevi and special-site naevi (see section Dysplastic naevus, and section Special-site naevi (of the breast, axilla, scalp, and ear)).

cards.title: Melanoma metastatic to the skin
cards.excerpt: Entity: Melanoma metastatic to the skin Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis of metastatic melanoma in the skin includes primary melanoma, primary dermal melanoma, and atypical naevus. Blue naevus–like metastases are difficult to distinguish from common or epithelioid blue naevus. The presence of cytologically atypical epithelioid melanocytes and mitotic figures can mimic blue naevus–like melanoma.

cards.title: Nodular melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Nodular melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis Unpigmented tumours must be distinguished from squamous cell carcinomas, appendageal tumours, sarcomas, and cutaneous lymphomas by immunohistochemistry. Melanoma metastases tend to have more mitoses or intravascular deposits of neoplastic melanocytes at the base.

cards.title: Invasive melanoma — ICD-10: C43 - malignant melanoma of skin
cards.excerpt:
Epidemiology
Incidence: 3.2 age standardized rate (world) (CA Cancer J Clin 2021;71:209)
~1.7% of global cancer (CA Cancer J Clin 2021;71:209)
Incidence has risen rapidly over the last 50 years (J Invest Dermatol 2009;129:1666)
Higher incidence in periequatorial zone (CA Cancer J Clin 2021;71:209)
M:F = 1.5:1 (SEER: Cancer Stat Facts - Melanoma of the Skin [Accessed 24 July 2025])

cards.title: Invasive melanoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Multistep process that involves interaction of genomic, environmental and host factors
4 step model proposed (Pigment Cell Melanoma Res 2016;29:122)
Mitogenic driver mutation (i.e., BRAF mutation)
Escaping primary senescence (i.e., CDKN2A loss)
Overcoming apoptosis (i.e., TP53 mutation)
Immortalization (i.e., TERTp mutation)

cards.title: Invasive melanoma — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Wide surgical excision with safety skin margins according to Breslow depth (Eur J Cancer 2025;215:115153, J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2024;22:290)
In situ: 0.5 cm safety skin margins
Breslow depth ≤ 2 mm: 1 cm
Breslow depth > 2 mm: 2 cm
Sentinel lymph node biopsy (staging procedure and prognostic value) (J Clin Oncol 2018;36:399)
Adjuvant / systemic therapy starting from stage III melanomas (J Clin Oncol 2023;41:4794)

who_cross_mentions.snippet: Entity: Nodular melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis Unpigmented tumours must be distinguished from squamous cell carcinomas, appendageal tumours, sarcomas, and cutaneous lymphomas by immunohistochemistry. Melanoma metastases tend to have more mitoses or intravascular deposits of neoplastic melanocytes at the base.

missing_essentials: Stromal changes: Variable inflammatory infiltrate (brisk, nonbrisk, absent) not stated clearly as a separate finding in Microscopic section.
Nuclear chromatin detail (peppered moth nuclei) is not specifically described in the Microscopic section, though hyperchromasia and pleomorphism are covered.
Explicit mention of increased serum LDH as a laboratory marker of advanced/metastatic disease is not in the Clinical Issues or Ancillary Tests section.
